fact: Digital Policy Alert records that the Supreme Council of Digital Society adopted the Cloud First Policy on 13 March 2024, requiring data classified top secret or secret to be hosted exclusively within Egypt.
Digital Policy Alert records that the Cloud First Policy (2024), including its data localisation requirement, entered into force on 22 August 2024.

The Cabinet's spokesperson said the Supreme Council for the Digital Society, at its first meeting after reconstitution under the Prime Minister, approved and launched the cloud computing policy, in line with the Digital Egypt strategy (document date is a proxy).

At a cabinet meeting chaired by the prime minister on 2026-09-20, the ICT minister said the ministry is preparing an integrated national data-centre strategy with other ministries and bodies to expand data centres and their capacity inside Egypt.

On 2026-09-08 the ICT minister said the ministry is developing a national data centre strategy covering storage and compute needs, investment, regulation and legislation, standards, sustainability, skills and digital sovereignty.
On 2026-07-21 the ICT minister said the ministry, with the bodies concerned, is preparing a national data-centre strategy as a core component of digital sovereignty.

On 2026-06-30 Al-Ahram reported the ICT ministry is preparing an integrated national strategy to regulate data-centre establishment, under presidential directives that include digital sovereignty and data localisation.

ICT minister Amr Talaat said Egypt launched its cloud-first policy through the Supreme Council for Digital Society, and that a top-level government committee hosted by MCIT has been formed to prepare a plan for state bodies, authorities and ministries to benefit from the policy.
